title: Hearing on senior centers located at NYCHA housing
summary: The Council's Aging and Public Housing Committees will hold a joint oversight hearing examining the condition and operation of older adult centers located on NYCHA property, including repair delays, unclear agency responsibilities between DFTA and NYCHA, and effects of the PACT privatization program. As of 2025 there were 109 such centers serving over 7,200 daily participants, with examples cited of centers closed for months or years due to unresolved maintenance issues. The committees will also consider Introduction 1083-2026, which would require DFTA to station a financial literacy advisor at each older adult center for at least 20 hours a month.
